fatal_errors: The hypothesis predicts that six-layer ESD coatings have better overall structural integrity than three-layer coatings, whereas the reported result was that six layers generally increased roughness, oxidation, pores, and superficial microfissuring despite improving coverage.

It asserts effective performance under aggressive operating conditions and mitigation relative to fusion-welding repair even though no corrosion, aggressive-environment, service-life, or direct fusion-welding comparison was performed.

The falsification experiment does not concretely specify the simulated aggressive exposure or include a traditional fusion-welded repair comparator, so it cannot test the central service-performance claim.
explanation: The response reconstructs the materials, SPS-to-ESD intervention, principal processing windows, and core diffusion/densification and spark-transfer mechanisms very closely. It also appropriately acknowledges that aggressive-environment effectiveness remains unvalidated. However, its main outcome claim combines two distinct comparisons and reverses the layer-count result: higher SPS temperature generally improved compact integrity, but increasing deposition from three to six layers did not generally improve coating quality and instead produced more oxidation, roughness, and microfissures. Claims of a mechanically robust bond, hot-cracking mitigation, and aggressive-service effectiveness extend beyond the reported measurements. The proposed SEM/EDS, XRD, density, hardness, and mass measurements can discriminate processing and microstructural effects, but they cannot establish superiority to fusion welding or durability in aggressive service without adhesion, mechanical integrity, corrosion/wear exposure, and fusion-repair controls. No external supporting evidence is cited.
